findings.title: enableSqlExpressions ignores the feature flag and always returns false
findings.body: The helper computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`, then returns false on both branches (`if enabled { return false }; return false`). The feature flag therefore has no effect, and the function reads as if it checks the flag when it does not. Any future change that re-enables SQL expressions by fixing only the stub in db.go would also need this function rewritten. The function should be replaced by a plain, explicit disable with a comment explaining why, or the flag check should be restored and gated behind the real implementation.

findings.title: SQL gate exists only in the reader; the security fix relies on the stub returning errors
findings.body: The only explicit disable is in ReadQuery's QueryTypeSQL branch. The exported UnmarshalSQLCommand in pkg/expr/sql_command.go (line ~68) calls NewSQLCommand directly, and SQLCommand.Execute (line ~96) runs db.QueryFramesInto with no check. The code is therefore safe only because sql.TablesList happens to fail through the stub RunCommands in db.go. If any caller builds a SQLCommand directly, or the stub is replaced with a real implementation, the SQL path is reachable again. The disable should be enforced at NewSQLCommand and/or Execute, not only in one reader branch.

findings.title: tablesFromAST indexes ast[0] without a length check
findings.body: tablesFromAST does `flatten.Flatten(ast[0], ...)`. If the JSON from the backend is an empty array, this panics with index out of range. The stub now means this path is unreachable in practice, but the function is still present and reachable from TablesList if the DB is ever reimplemented. A length check is needed before indexing.

findings.title: Stub DB silently replaces the real engine; parser JSON path is now dead code
findings.body: DB.TablesList, RunCommands and QueryFramesInto all return 'not implemented' errors. Nothing documents that this is a deliberate security stub, and the TablesList parsing in parser.go (including the rawSQL quote-escaping and the json_serialize_sql logic) is now dead code that no test exercises. A maintainer reading this later could mistake the stub for a missing implementation and re-enable it without the required review. A comment stating the reason and the intended re-enable conditions is needed.

findings.title: No tests added or updated for the disabled SQL expression behaviour
findings.body: The PR changes SQL expression behaviour from functional to always-rejected, but no test was added to assert that a SQL query type returns an error, and existing SQL-related tests in pkg/expr were not updated. Without a regression test, a future change could re-enable SQL execution silently. The PR description also notes the feature-flag documentation was not updated, so the flag now does nothing while still appearing in the feature toggle list.
